title: Lost variety of the 1960s and 70s cultural influences
summary: In the 60s and 70s bossa nova, samba and other styles melded with jazz; he sees less variety today.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: Is jazz healthy? Young players, rock and the future

blocks.x: styles of music were out there, and a lot of them, you know the bossa nova, sambas, all these things melded very well with jazz. Well today we don’t have that variety of different cultures coming into jazz. Somebody will argue with me yes there are some European or world music things that have creeped in. But we don’t have, you know we had the straight eighth stuff, we had the samba stuff, we had, you name it, all kinds of different styles of music that could be absorbed in jazz, Afro-Cuban, all that stuff. But today I don’t see that wealth of other styles that can be melded into a large ensemble or into jazz. Now maybe I’m not listening as much as I used to, I probably don’t listen as much as I used to, but you know I have the XM radio jazz station and I listen to other stations, and try to keep current. But it’s hard to come up with something original when you don’t have to. Put it this way, I don’t have a deadline, I don’t have a bandleader breathing down my neck, where’s the chart, where’s the chart. So that’s an answer.
